question: In triangle ABC, BD perp AC at D and angle DBC = 14circ. E is a point on BC such that angle CAE = 75circ. What is the measure of angle AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled ΔBDC, ∠C = 180° − (90° + 14°) = 76°.

In ΔACE, since B-E-C is a straight line, ∠AEB acts as the exterior angle at vertex E.

By the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠C + ∠CAE

⇒ ∠AEB = 76° + 75° = 151°.

**∴ The correct answer is 151°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

BD ⊥ AC at D ⇒ ∠BDC = 90°

∠DBC = 14°

∠CAE = 75°

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔBDC, the sum of the angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (∠BDC + ∠DBC)

⇒ ∠C = 180° − (90° + 14°) = 76°

⇒ Now, considering ΔACE, the sum of the angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (∠C + ∠CAE)

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − (76° + 75°)

⇒ ∠AEC = 180° − 151° = 29°

⇒ Since point E lies on the straight line segment BC, angles ∠AEB and ∠AEC form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠AEB + ∠AEC = 180°

⇒ ∠AEB = 180° − 29° = 151°

**∴ The correct answer is 151°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. This helps in directly finding angles without calculating the third interior angle first.

Linear Pair Axiom

When two adjacent angles are formed by a pair of intersecting lines or on a straight line, their sum is exactly 180°.

Sum of Angles of a Triangle

The sum of all three interior angles in any Euclidean triangle always equals exactly 180°. In a right triangle, the two non-right angles sum up to exactly 90°.
